summary: Zinc contributes to immune function, protein and DNA synthesis, growth, wound healing and taste.

functions.title: Physiological role
functions.description: Zinc contributes to immune function, protein and DNA synthesis, growth, wound healing and taste.

functions.title: Food context
functions.description: Animal foods, beans, nuts, whole grains, eggs and dairy foods contain zinc.

referenceValues.notes: FDA label reference for adults and children aged 4+. Not a personalised target, EAR, RDA or UL.

foodSourceRules.notes: Comparable source-backed composition per 100 g; not a health score or a measure of individual absorption.

absorptionFactors.description: Phytates in beans and grains can reduce zinc absorption; vegetarian or vegan food-composition totals do not establish absorbed zinc.

deficiency.overview: Zinc deficiency can impair growth or wound healing and affect taste; these features have other possible causes.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: Long-term excessive zinc intake can lower copper status and impair immunity; more zinc is not automatically better.
excess.medicalBoundary: An upper limit is not an intake goal. Seek medical or professional advice before changing supplement or medication use.
